questions.question_english: A school Principal needs to purchase dual desks worth Rs. 1,50,000/- for classrooms. According to GFR 2017, what is the most appropriate procurement method if the required items are certified as not available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)?
options_english: Direct cash purchase from a single nearby vendor without seeking competitive quotations.
Publishing an Advertised Tender Enquiry across leading national newspapers and public portals.
Single Tender Enquiry awarded directly to an unverified local furniture supplier.
Procurement through a Local Purchase Committee comprising three members as approved by the competent authority.
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 155 of GFR 2017 ('Purchase of goods by Purchase Committee'), purchase of goods costing above Rs. 25,000/- and up to Rs. 2,50,000/- on each occasion may be carried out on the recommendations of a duly constituted Local Purchase Committee (LPC) consisting of three members appointed by the Head of Department/Competent Authority. When the goods are not available on GeM, the committee conducts an offline or local market survey to identify suitable suppliers, ascertains price reasonableness and quality, obtains quotations, and prepares a joint survey certificate before recommending the purchase. Since Rs. 1,50,000/- falls squarely between Rs. 25,000 and Rs. 2,50,000, procurement via a 3-member Local Purchase Committee is the exact prescribed procedure.
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 155 ('क्रय समिति द्वारा माल की खरीद') के अनुसार, प्रत्येक अवसर पर ₹25,000/- से अधिक और ₹2,50,000/- तक की लागत वाली वस्तुओं की खरीद विभागाध्यक्ष/सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा गठित तीन सदस्यों की एक 'स्थानीय क्रय समिति' (LPC) की सिफारिश पर की जा सकती है। यदि वस्तुएं GeM पर उपलब्ध नहीं हैं, तो यह समिति बाजार सर्वेक्षण करती है, प्रतिष्ठित आपूर्तिकर्ताओं से दरों का पता लगाती है, गुणवत्ता और मूल्य की औचित्यता की जांच करती है तथा संयुक्त प्रमाण पत्र तैयार करके खरीद की सिफारिश करती है। चूँकि ₹1,50,000/- की राशि ₹25,000 से ₹2.5 लाख के मध्य आती है, अतः तीन सदस्यीय स्थानीय क्रय समिति के माध्यम से खरीद करना ही नियमानुकूल प्रक्रिया है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Purchase through a Local Purchase Committee of three members as decided by Head of Department.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Committee of three members as decided by Head of Department. For procuring goods valued above twenty-five thousand rupees and up to two lakh fifty thousand rupees on each occasion when not available on GeM, Rule 155 mandates purchase through a three-member Local Purchase Committee. The committee conducts a local market survey, evaluates suitable suppliers, certifies quality and price reasonableness, and jointly recommends the most appropriate purchase offer.

questions.question_english: Under Rule 170 of GFR 2017, what is the standard percentage range of the estimated value of goods that must be demanded as Bid Security (Earnest Money Deposit - EMD) from participating bidders?
questions.explanation_english: Rule 170 of GFR 2017 prescribes the provisions for 'Bid Security' (Earnest Money Deposit - EMD). To safeguard against frivolous or irresponsible bidders withdrawing or altering their bids during the bid validity period, procuring authorities obtain Bid Security from bidders. The amount of Bid Security should ordinarily range between two percent to five percent (2% to 5%) of the estimated value of the goods to be procured. The bid security may be accepted in the form of Account Payee Demand Draft, Fixed Deposit Receipt, Banker's Cheque, or Bank Guarantee. Note that Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) registered with designated bodies (Udyam Registration) and Startups recognized by DPIIT are exempted from submitting Bid Security (Rule 170(i)).
questions.explanation_hindi: GFR 2017 के नियम 170 के अनुसार 'बोली सुरक्षा' (Bid Security / बयाना राशि - EMD) का प्रावधान गैर-गंभीर या लापरवाह बोलीदाताओं को बोली वैधता अवधि के दौरान हटने से रोकने के लिए किया जाता है। नियम 170 के तहत बोली सुरक्षा की राशि सामान्यतः खरीदे जाने वाले माल के अनुमानित मूल्य के 2% से 5% के बीच निर्धारित की जानी चाहिए। यह राशि अकाउंट पेयी डिमांड ड्राफ्ट, सावधि जमा रसीद (FDR), बैंकर चेक या बैंक गारंटी के रूप में स्वीकार की जा सकती है। उल्लेखनीय है कि सूक्ष्म एवं लघु उद्यमों (MSEs) तथा DPIIT द्वारा मान्यता प्राप्त स्टार्टअप्स को नियम 170(i) के तहत EMD जमा करने से छूट प्राप्त होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 2% to 5%

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 170 of the General Financial Rules mandates that procuring authorities obtain Bid Security, also known as Earnest Money Deposit, from participating bidders to safeguard against frivolous or non-serious bids. The standard bid security amount ranges between two percent and five percent of the estimated procurement value, deposited via approved banking instruments like demand drafts or bank guarantees.

questions.question_hindi: आईटी प्रयोगशाला (IT Lab) के भौतिक सत्यापन (Physical Verification) के दौरान सत्यापन समिति को पता चलता है कि दो डेस्कटॉप मॉनिटर गायब हैं। जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियमों के अनुसार इस निष्कर्ष का तात्कालिक परिणाम क्या होगा?
options_hindi: गायब मॉनिटरों को बिना किसी औपचारिक प्रशासनिक प्रक्रिया के स्टॉक रजिस्टर से स्वतः ही हटा दिया जाता है।
भौतिक सत्यापन समिति के सदस्यों को गायब मॉनिटरों की क्रय लागत का व्यक्तिगत रूप से भुगतान करना होगा।
कमी को छिपाने के लिए विद्यालय प्रशासन को स्थानीय/छात्र निधि से चुपचाप प्रतिस्थापन मॉनिटर खरीदने होंगे।
विसंगति (Discrepancy) को तुरंत अभिलिखित किया जाना चाहिए और कार्यालयाध्यक्ष (Head of Office) को जिम्मेदारी तय करने के लिए जांच शुरू करनी चाहिए।

questions.question_english: During the physical verification of an IT laboratory, the verification committee discovers that two desktop monitors are missing. What is the immediate procedural requirement under GFR 2017 regarding this finding?
options_english: The missing monitors are automatically struck off from the register without any formal administrative procedure.
The members of the physical verification committee must personally reimburse the purchase cost of the missing monitors.
The school administration must silently purchase replacement monitors using local school funds to cover up the shortage.
The discrepancy must be formally recorded and the Head of Office must initiate an inquiry to fix responsibility.
questions.explanation_english: As per Rule 213 and Rule 214 of General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, along with Rule 33 and Rule 34 concerning reports of losses, any shortage, loss, or discrepancy discovered during the physical verification of fixed assets or stores must be immediately recorded in the physical verification report and brought to the notice of the Head of Office (HOO) / competent authority. The Head of Office (e.g., School Principal) is duty-bound to initiate an immediate administrative inquiry to ascertain the cause of the loss (whether due to theft, fraud, or negligence), fix responsibility on the defaulting custodian/custody officer, and process the matter either for recovery or formal write-off under the Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR). Striking off assets arbitrarily or covering shortages by unapproved purchases is illegal under financial regulations.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 213 और 214 के साथ पठित नियम 33 एवं 34 (हानियों की रिपोर्ट) के अनुसार, अचल परिसंपत्तियों या भंडार के भौतिक सत्यापन के दौरान पाई गई किसी भी प्रकार की कमी, क्षति या विसंगति को भौतिक सत्यापन रिपोर्ट में विधिवत दर्ज किया जाना अनिवार्य है। कार्यालयाध्यक्ष (जैसे विद्यालय के प्राचार्य) का यह विधिक दायित्व है कि वे इस विसंगति को संज्ञान में लेकर तुरंत एक प्रशासनिक जांच शुरू करें, ताकि हानि के वास्तविक कारणों (चोरी, कपट या घोर उपेक्षा) का पता लगाया जा सके, संबंधित स्टॉक अभिरक्षक पर उत्तरदायित्व निर्धारित किया जा सके, तथा वित्तीय अधिकार प्रत्यायोजन नियमों (DFPR) के तहत वसूली या अपलेखन (write-off) की प्रक्रिया प्रारंभ की जा सके। किसी भी सरकारी सामग्री को बिना जांच के रजिस्टर से हटाना या गुप्त रूप से प्रतिस्थापन करना वित्तीय नियमों का गंभीर उल्लंघन है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The discrepancy must be recorded and the Head of Office must initiate an inquiry to fix responsibility.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Head of Office must initiate an inquiry to fix responsibility. When physical verification reveals missing non-consumable assets, the verification committee must document the discrepancy in the verification report. The Head of Office is required to initiate an immediate administrative inquiry to investigate the cause of the loss, fix responsibility for negligence, and initiate formal recovery or write-off procedures under financial rules.

questions.question_english: Which of the following actions represents a direct violation of the canon of financial propriety requiring that "expenditure should not be prima facie more than the occasion demands"?
options_english: Procuring standardized laboratory equipment for secondary classes at GeM-approved rates
Booking a banquet hall in a luxury five-star hotel using government school funds to conduct a routine staff meeting
Paying the standard government electricity tariffs for the school building
Purchasing necessary first-aid and medical supplies for the school infirmary
questions.explanation_english:
Booking an expensive five-star hotel for a routine staff meeting represents a blatant breach of Rule 21(ii) of GFR 2017, which mandates that "The expenditure should not be prima facie more than the occasion demands."

Analysis:
1. Extravagance vs Economy: A routine administrative meeting requires a standard, modest meeting room. Hosting it in a luxury commercial hotel using public educational funds is grossly disproportionate to the administrative occasion, especially when school halls or departmental premises are available at no extra cost.
2. Legitimate Expenditures: Purchasing lab equipment, paying utility bills, and stocking first-aid supplies are essential, cost-controlled, and proportionate expenditures that satisfy the standards of financial propriety.
questions.explanation_hindi:
एक नियमित स्टाफ बैठक के लिए एक महंगे पांच सितारा होटल को बुक करना GFR 2017 के नियम 21(ii) का खुला उल्लंघन है, जो यह निर्धारित करता है कि "व्यय प्रथम दृष्टया अवसर की मांग से अधिक नहीं होना चाहिए।"

विश्लेषण:
1. अपव्यय बनाम मितव्ययिता: एक सामान्य प्रशासनिक बैठक के लिए एक साधारण बैठक कक्ष पर्याप्त होता है। सरकारी विद्यालय कोष से लग्जरी होटल में ऐसी बैठक आयोजित करना अवसर की तुलना में अत्यधिक और असंगत व्यय है, विशेषकर जब विद्यालय सभागार बिना किसी अतिरिक्त लागत के उपलब्ध हो।
2. वैध व्यय: प्रयोगशाला उपकरण खरीदना, उपयोगिता बिलों का भुगतान करना और प्राथमिक उपचार सामग्री रखना आवश्यक, लागत-नियंत्रित और आनुपातिक व्यय हैं जो वित्तीय औचित्य की कसौटी पर खरे उतरते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Organizing a routine staff meeting in a five- star hotel using school funds.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: star hotel using school funds. Hosting a routine departmental staff meeting in an expensive luxury venue represents an extravagant expenditure that clearly exceeds what the occasion reasonably demands. Standards of financial propriety require maintaining strict economy and choosing cost-effective options for public business. Unnecessary lavish spending of public funds on basic routine administrative functions constitutes a direct violation of fundamental financial propriety principles.

questions.question_english: Which of the following represents a recognized exception to the general rule that condemned items must be sold through commercial bidding to generate public revenue?
options_english: Intact historic brass artifacts declared functionally obsolete by administrative executive orders.
Unserviceable government motor vehicles that have exceeded their prescribed operational lifespan.
Old broken wooden furniture items that can no longer be repaired for classroom use.
Highly classified, sensitive, or security documents that must be destroyed/shredded rather than sold publicly.
questions.explanation_english: While GFR 2017 generally mandates that unserviceable assets and scrap be sold via tender or auction to realize revenue for the exchequer (Rule 218), Rule 222 and departmental security instructions provide an explicit exception for classified, secret, or confidential records, confidential examination materials (such as question papers/used answer sheets after prescribed retention periods), and security-sensitive items. To prevent breaches of national security, institutional confidentiality, or personal privacy, such documents must be pulped, shredded, or incinerated under the direct supervision of a gazetted officer, rather than offered for public sale or commercial recycling.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्यतः जीएफआर (GFR), 2017 के नियम 218 के तहत कंडम संपत्ति और कबाड़ को सार्वजनिक राजस्व अर्जित करने के लिए बेचा जाता है। किंतु जीएफआर के नियम 222 तथा सरकारी सुरक्षा नियमों के अनुसार अति गोपनीय, संवेदनशील या सुरक्षा संबंधी दस्तावेज (जैसे परीक्षा संबंधी गोपनीय अभिलेख, गोपनीय पत्राचार आदि) इसका अनिवार्य अपवाद हैं। गोपनीयता और सुरक्षा के उल्लंघन को रोकने के उद्देश्य से ऐसे संवेदनशील दस्तावेजों को व्यावसायिक रूप से बेचने के बजाय एक राजपत्रित अधिकारी की प्रत्यक्ष देखरेख में कतरकर (shredding), लुगदी बनाकर (pulping) या जलाकर नष्ट करना आवश्यक होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Highly classified or security documents which must be destroyed/shredded without public sale.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: must be destroyed/shredded without public sale. While condemned property is generally sold to generate public revenue, highly classified, sensitive, or security-restricted documents represent a clear exception. To prevent unauthorized disclosure of confidential information, security regulations require that such sensitive papers be destroyed or shredded under official supervision rather than offered for public sale or commercial recycling.

सामान्य वित्तीय नियमावली (GFR), 2017 के अंतर्गत अनुबंध के मानक प्रपत्रों (Standard Forms of Contract) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 225(i) and (ii) of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, standard forms of contract must be adopted in all public procurements wherever feasible and available. questions.explanation_english: In government works and procurement under GFR and standard Works Manuals, a 'Lump-sum Contract' is an agreement under which a contractor undertakes to execute a complete and accurately defined scope of work or project in accordance with detailed plans and specifications for a single, fixed all-inclusive total sum. Payment is released either upon complete satisfactory finishing or in pre-agreed milestone stages, provided the original design and specifications remain unchanged. Hence, option A accurately defines a lump-sum contract.

Assertion (A): A second advance for Travelling Allowance (TA) should not normally be granted to a government servant until an account has been rendered and adjusted for the first advance.
Reason (R): Immediate and timely adjustment of advances is essential to prevent unauthorized accumulation of public money in the hands of individuals and to prevent misappropriation.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 291 of GFR 2017 and general principles of government financial accounting:
- Assertion (A) is true: Financial rules explicitly dictate that no second advance for travel or other official purposes should normally be granted to an employee while a previous advance remains outstanding and unadjusted. Sanctioning overlapping advances without settlement of prior accounts is a grave procedural irregularity.
- Reason (R) is true: The foundational rationale for this restriction is financial prudence and internal audit control. Allowing advances to remain unadjusted results in unauthorized retention and accumulation of government cash in private hands, increasing the risk of loss, cash hoarding, and fraudulent misappropriation of public funds.
Moreover, Reason (R) provides the exact logical and regulatory justification for why Assertion (A) is strictly enforced.
Therefore, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question_english:
Consider the following yardsticks laid down under Rule 144 of GFR 2017 (Fundamental principles of public buying):

I. The specifications in terms of quality and type should meet the basic needs of the organization without including superfluous features.
II. Care should be taken to avoid purchasing quantities in excess of genuine requirement to prevent inventory lock-up.
III. Offers should be invited following a fair, transparent, and reasonable procedure.
IV. Technical specifications should be drawn up in a restrictive manner to limit the bidding exclusively to a preferred single brand.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III only
II, III and IV only
I, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I, II, and III are correct, whereas Statement IV directly violates Rule 144.

Statutory Mandate under Rule 144 of GFR 2017:
1. Objective Specifications (Rule 144(i)(a)): The description of the subject matter of procurement must be objective, functional, and meet the basic needs of the organization without incorporating superfluous or luxury features.
2. Prohibition of Brand Bias (Rule 144(i)(b)): Technical specifications shall NOT indicate a requirement for a particular trademark, trade name, patent, design, origin, or specific producer unless there is no other sufficiently precise way of describing the requirements (and even then, words like "or equivalent" must be included). Tailoring specifications to favor a single vendor/brand is prohibited.
3. Quantity Control (Rule 144(ii)): Over-purchasing leads to wastage and inventory holding costs.
4. Transparency (Rule 144(iii)): Procurement must be conducted through an open, transparent, and non-discriminatory competitive process.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I, II और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन IV नियम 144 का सीधा उल्लंघन करता है।

GFR 2017 के नियम 144 के तहत वैधानिक अधिदेश:
1. वस्तुनिष्ठ विनिर्देश (नियम 144(i)(a)): खरीद की विषय-वस्तु का विवरण वस्तुनिष्ठ और कार्यात्मक होना चाहिए, जो बिना किसी अनावश्यक या विलासितापूर्ण विशेषताओं के संगठन की बुनियादी जरूरतों को पूरा करे।
2. ब्रांड पक्षपात का निषेध (नियम 144(i)(b)): तकनीकी विनिर्देशों में किसी विशेष ट्रेडमार्क, ब्रांड नाम, पेटेंट, डिजाइन या विशिष्ट निर्माता का उल्लेख नहीं होना चाहिए, जिससे प्रतिस्पर्धा प्रतिबंधित होती हो। किसी एक विक्रेता/ब्रांड को लाभ पहुंचाने के लिए विनिर्देश तैयार करना पूरी तरह प्रतिबंधित है।
3. मात्रा नियंत्रण (नियम 144(ii)): वास्तविक आवश्यकता से अधिक खरीद करने से बर्बादी और पूंजी अवरुद्ध होती है।
4. पारदर्शिता (नियम 144(iii)): खरीद प्रक्रिया खुली, पारदर्शी और गैर-भेदभावपूर्ण प्रतिस्पर्धी प्रणाली के माध्यम से आयोजित की जानी चाहिए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Public procurement yardsticks mandate that technical specifications meet actual organizational requirements without including unnecessary, restrictive, or luxurious features. Procuring authorities must avoid purchasing quantities exceeding actual needs and must invite offers through transparent, competitive procedures. Drawing up specifications to favor or restrict bidding to a single brand is strictly prohibited, as procurement must remain open and non-discriminatory.

questions.question_hindi:
गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस (GeM) पर खरीद सीमाओं (वित्तीय सीमाओं) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. ₹25,000 तक की खरीद GeM पर उपलब्ध किसी भी आपूर्तिकर्ता के माध्यम से की जा सकती है, बशर्ते वह वांछित गुणवत्ता, विनिर्देश और वितरण अवधि को पूरा करता हो।

IV. केंद्र सरकार के मंत्रालयों और विभागों के लिए GeM के माध्यम से खरीद करना वैकल्पिक (ऐच्छिक) है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_hindi: I, II और III
I, III और IV
II, III और IV
I, II, III और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding procurement limits on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM):
I. Purchases up to Rs. 25,000 can be made through any of the available suppliers on GeM meeting the requisite quality, specification, and delivery period.
II. Purchases above Rs. 25,000 and up to Rs. 5,00,000 should be made through the L1 (lowest) bidder among available suppliers of at least three different manufacturers.
III. Purchases above Rs. 5,00,000 mandatorily require online bidding or reverse auction on GeM.
IV. Procurement through GeM is optional for Ministries and Departments of the Central Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III
I, III and IV
II, III and IV
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 149 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017, procurement of common-use goods and services through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is mandatory, not optional, for all Central Government Ministries, Departments, and attached/subordinate offices, including educational institutions like Kendriya Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas. Rule 149 prescribes strict threshold-based procurement procedures:
1. Direct Purchase (Up to Rs. 25,000): The buyer can procure directly from any available supplier on GeM whose product meets requisite quality, technical specifications, and delivery period.
2. L1 Comparison (Above Rs. 25,000 up to Rs. 5,00,000): The buyer must compare available products from at least three different manufacturers on GeM and select the lowest cost (L1) bidder that satisfies technical requirements.
3. Mandatory Online Bidding / e-Reverse Auction (Above Rs. 5,00,000): The procurement must mandatorily be conducted through online bidding or reverse auction tools integrated into GeM.
Because GeM is statutory and mandatory under GFR Rule 149, Statement IV is incorrect. Statements I, II, and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 149 के अनुसार, केंद्र सरकार के सभी मंत्रालयों, विभागों तथा उनके अधीनस्थ कार्यालयों (जिनमें केंद्रीय विद्यालय एवं नवोदय विद्यालय जैसे स्वायत्त निकाय भी शामिल हैं) के लिए GeM (गवर्नमेंट ई-मार्केटप्लेस) पर उपलब्ध सामान्य उपयोग की वस्तुओं और सेवाओं की खरीद करना अनिवार्य है, न कि वैकल्पिक। नियम 149 के अंतर्गत वित्तीय सीमाएं इस प्रकार निर्धारित हैं:
1. ₹25,000 तक: वांछित गुणवत्ता, तकनीकी विनिर्देश और वितरण अवधि को पूरा करने वाले GeM पर उपलब्ध किसी भी विक्रेता से सीधी खरीद की जा सकती है।
2. ₹25,000 से अधिक तथा ₹5,00,000 तक: GeM पर उपलब्ध कम से कम तीन अलग-अलग निर्माताओं के उत्पादों की तुलना करके सबसे कम मूल्य (L1) वाले योग्य विक्रेता का चयन करना अनिवार्य है।
3. ₹5,00,000 से अधिक: GeM पर उपलब्ध ऑनलाइन बिडिंग (बोली) या ई-रिवर्स ऑक्शन (e-Reverse Auction) उपकरण के माध्यम से ही खरीद की जानी अनिवार्य है।
चूंकि GeM से खरीद करना मंत्रालयों/विभागों के लिए अनिवार्य है, अतः कथन IV गलत है। कथन I, II और III सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: GeM rules establish structured purchase thresholds: direct purchase up to twenty-five thousand rupees, mandatory comparison among at least three different manufacturers to select the lowest bidder for values up to five lakh rupees, and mandatory online bidding or reverse auction above five lakh rupees. Crucially, GeM procurement is mandatory, not optional, for central government entities.

I. तकनीकी और वित्तीय बोलियों का मूल्यांकन

III. अनुबंध प्रदान करना और खरीद आदेश (Purchase Order) जारी करना
IV. निविदा सूचना का प्रकाशन और बोलियां आमंत्रित करना

questions.question_english:
Arrange the following sequential stages of a standard public procurement cycle under GFR 2017 in the correct chronological order:
I. Evaluation of technical and financial bids
II. Assessment of need and formulation of technical specifications
III. Award of contract and issuance of purchase order
IV. Publication of tender notice and invitation of bids
options_english: II, IV, I, III
IV, II, I, III
II, I, IV, III
IV, I, II, III
questions.explanation_english:
A standard public procurement cycle under GFR 2017 and procurement manuals follows a strict chronological workflow:
1. Stage II (Need & Specifications): The procuring entity determines the precise institutional need, checks budget availability, and frames generic, objective technical specifications (Rule 144).
2. Stage IV (Tender Publication): The bid document is issued and published on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) or GeM to invite offers (Rule 161/162).
3. Stage I (Bid Evaluation): Submitted bids are opened publicly, evaluated by a designated tender committee on technical and financial grounds against the pre-disclosed criteria (Rule 163/173).
4. Stage III (Contract Award): The competent financial authority approves the recommendation of the lowest evaluated responsive bidder (L1) and issues the formal contract/purchase order (Rule 173(xxi)).
Therefore, the correct chronological order is II -> IV -> I -> III.
questions.explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 और खरीद नियमावली के अंतर्गत सार्वजनिक खरीद प्रक्रिया का सही कालानुक्रमिक चरण इस प्रकार होता है:
1. चरण II (आवश्यकता और विनिर्देश निर्धारण): सर्वप्रथम संस्थागत आवश्यकता का निर्धारण, बजट की उपलब्धता की जांच और गैर-स्वामित्व वाले सामान्य तकनीकी विनिर्देश तैयार किए जाते हैं (नियम 144)।
2. चरण IV (निविदा आमंत्रण): निविदा सूचना तैयार करके CPPP पोर्टल, वेबसाइट या GeM पर प्रकाशित की जाती है ताकि बोलियां आमंत्रित की जा सकें (नियम 161/162)।
3. चरण I (बोलियों का मूल्यांकन): प्राप्त बोलियों को सार्वजनिक रूप से खोला जाता है और निविदा समिति द्वारा पूर्व-निर्धारित मानदंडों पर तकनीकी एवं वित्तीय मूल्यांकन किया जाता है (नियम 163/173)।
4. चरण III (अनुबंध प्रदान करना): सक्षम प्राधिकारी के अनुमोदनोपरांत सफल न्यूनतम उत्तरदायी बोलीदाता (L1) को अनुबंध प्रदान किया जाता है और आपूर्ति आदेश जारी किया जाता है।
अतः सही क्रम II -> IV -> I -> III है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) II, IV, I, III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The standard procurement cycle follows a systematic chronological order. First, the procuring entity determines operational requirements and frames technical specifications. Next, the entity publishes the tender invitation to attract vendor offers. Following tender submission, the committee systematically evaluates technical and financial bids against pre-established criteria. Finally, the competent authority approves the selection and issues the formal contract award.

options_english: The Controlling Officer

questions.explanation_english:
Under GFR 2017 (Rules 10, 52, and 67), the Controlling Officer holds primary administrative and supervisory responsibility for public expenditure within their department or division.

Key Responsibilities of a Controlling Officer:
1. Ensuring Propriety and Regularity: The Controlling Officer must verify that all Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) functioning under their supervision strictly observe the Canons of Financial Propriety, adhere to delegated financial powers, and follow accounting rules.
2. Budgetary Control: They must ensure expenditure does not exceed sanctioned grants and that allocations are utilized for the purposes intended by Parliament/Government.
3. Institutional Context: In educational directorates, the Deputy Director of Education or Regional Officer acts as the Controlling Officer overseeing school Principals (DDOs).
questions.explanation_hindi:
GFR 2017 (नियम 10, 52 और 67) के तहत, नियंत्रक अधिकारी (Controlling Officer) अपने विभाग या प्रभाग के भीतर सार्वजनिक व्यय की प्राथमिक प्रशासनिक और पर्यवेक्षी जिम्मेदारी संभालता है।

नियंत्रक अधिकारी के मुख्य दायित्व:
1. औचित्य और नियमितता सुनिश्चित करना: नियंत्रक अधिकारी को यह सत्यापित करना होता है कि उसके पर्यवेक्षण में कार्यरत सभी आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDOs) वित्तीय औचित्य के नियमों का कड़ाई से पालन करें, प्रत्यायोजित वित्तीय शक्तियों का उल्लंघन न करें और लेखा नियमों का पालन करें।
2. बजटीय नियंत्रण: उन्हें यह सुनिश्चित करना होता है कि व्यय स्वीकृत बजट अनुदानों से अधिक न हो और धन का उपयोग उसी उद्देश्य के लिए किया जाए जिसके लिए संसद/सरकार द्वारा इसे स्वीकृत किया गया था।
3. संस्थागत संदर्भ: शिक्षा निदेशालयों में, उप शिक्षा निदेशक (DDE) या क्षेत्रीय अधिकारी नियंत्रक अधिकारी के रूप में कार्य करते हैं जो विद्यालय प्राचार्यों (DDOs) के वित्तीय कामकाज की निगरानी करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The Controlling Officer

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Controlling Officer is primarily responsible for monitoring and supervising the financial conduct of all disbursing officers placed under their administrative jurisdiction. This responsibility includes verifying that subordinate officers strictly observe the principles of financial propriety, remain within allocated budget limits, maintain accurate accounts, submit timely financial returns, and prevent any unauthorized, wasteful, or illegal expenditure of public funds.

questions.question_hindi: आंतरिक लेखापरीक्षा रिपोर्ट (Internal Audit Report) के निपटान एवं अनुवर्ती कार्रवाई के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन गलत (INCORRECT) है?

कार्यालय प्रमुख (Head of Office) से यह अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वह उठाए गए सभी ऑडिट पैराग्राफों पर एक विस्तृत अनुपालन या की गई कार्रवाई रिपोर्ट (ATR) प्रस्तुत करे।

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the procedure for handling and follow-up of an Internal Audit Report?
options_english: The audit report systematically highlights procedural deviations, financial irregularities, and internal control weaknesses.
The Head of Office is expected to submit a detailed compliance or Action Taken Report (ATR) addressing all raised audit paragraphs.
All audit objections raised must be ignored if they relate to amounts under Rs. 10,000.
Unsettled serious audit paragraphs may eventually be escalated directly to the Head of the Department for disciplinary or administrative consideration.
questions.explanation_english: Statement C is incorrect because there is no provision in government financial accounting or the General Financial Rules (GFR) that permits an establishment to ignore audit objections merely on grounds of a low monetary threshold. Internal audit functions as an integral managerial control and surveillance mechanism designed to detect systemic procedural deviations, accounting errors, non-compliance with rules, and potential embezzlement. Even an objection involving an amount under Rs. 10,000 may reflect a breakdown of internal check systems, unauthorized expenditure, or recurring leakages. Therefore, the Head of Office (HOO) or Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) must submit a prompt, para-wise Action Taken Report (ATR) / compliance reply for every single audit query. Persistently unresolved or grave audit paras are brought to the notice of the Head of Department (HOD) for appropriate remedial and disciplinary action.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन C गलत है क्योंकि सरकारी लेखांकन नियमों अथवा जीएफआर (GFR) में ऐसा कोई नियम नहीं है जो किसी ऑडिट आपत्ति को केवल कम राशि (जैसे ₹10,000 से कम) होने के आधार पर अनदेखा करने की अनुमति देता हो। आंतरिक लेखापरीक्षा (Internal Audit) प्रशासन का एक अनिवार्य आंतरिक नियंत्रण तंत्र है, जिसका उद्देश्य प्रक्रियागत कमियों, वित्तीय अनियमितताओं, खातों की त्रुटियों तथा गबन की संभावनाओं को उजागर करना है। ₹10,000 से कम का आक्षेप भी आंतरिक नियंत्रण प्रणाली की विफलता या लगातार होने वाली प्रक्रियागत अनियमितता का संकेत हो सकता है। अतः कार्यालय प्रमुख (Head of Office) या आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) के लिए उठाए गए प्रत्येक ऑडिट पैराग्राफ पर विस्तृत अनुपालन आख्या / कार्रवाई रिपोर्ट (ATR) प्रस्तुत करना अनिवार्य है। अनिस्तारित गंभीर आक्षेपों को सुधारात्मक व अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई हेतु विभागाध्यक्ष (HOD) को भेजा जाता है।

questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 322(3) of GFR 2017 and Central Government Account (Receipts and Payments) Rules:
- Assertion (A) is true: Every administrative officer who holds a permanent advance (imprest) is required under statutory rules to formally send an acknowledgment of the exact amount of the advance held by them to the Accounts Officer on the 1st of April each financial year (as well as whenever there is a transfer of administrative charge).
- Reason (R) is true: An imprest involves public funds kept permanently outside the treasury chest under the immediate physical custody of the DDO. Annual acknowledgment acts as a primary audit verification tool to ensure that the physical cash plus valid unrecouped vouchers equal the total sanctioned advance at the opening of the fiscal year, preventing unrecorded deficits, embezzlement, or unauthorized retention.
Reason (R) provides the exact regulatory objective and direct explanation for why Assertion (A) is mandated.

questions.explanation_english: Rule 218 of GFR 2017 outlines the modes of disposal of surplus, obsolete, or unserviceable goods: (i) Advertised tender or public auction (Rule 218(1)(i)); (ii) Inviting quotations from scrap dealers when the assessed residual value is negligible or below prescribed limits (Rule 218(1)(ii)); and (iii) Hazardous and electronic waste must be disposed of strictly in compliance with statutory rules such as the E-Waste (Management) Rules issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) through authorized dismantlers/recyclers. questions.question_english: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding the classification, maintenance, and handling of stores under GFR 2017.
options_english: Items such as office stationery, laboratory chemicals, and cleaning supplies are classified as consumable stores.
Computers, office furniture, and scientific apparatus are classified as non-consumable stores / fixed assets.
Non-consumable stores are written off and struck off from the asset register as soon as they are issued to an employee.

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 211 of GFR 2017, non-consumable stores encompass durable goods (e.g., computers, furniture, scientific instruments, sports gear). When such items are issued to a staff member, teacher, or department, it represents merely a transfer of operational/physical custody recorded through an internal issue register or custody receipt; it DOES NOT permit striking off or writing off the asset from the master Stock Register. A non-consumable item remains on the institution's books as a government asset throughout its useful life until it is surveyed by a condemnation board, declared surplus/unserviceable/obsolete under Rule 217-219, and formally written off by the competent financial authority. Hence, statement (C) is completely incorrect.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियम (GFR), 2017 के नियम 211 के अनुसार, गैर-उपभोज्य भंडार (Non-consumable stores) में टिकाऊ वस्तुएं जैसे कंप्यूटर, फर्नीचर, प्रयोगशाला उपकरण आदि शामिल होते हैं। जब ये वस्तुएं किसी कर्मचारी या विभाग को उपयोग हेतु जारी की जाती हैं, तो यह केवल भौतिक अभिरक्षा (Custody) का अंतरण होता है। इसे स्टॉक रजिस्टर से हटाया या बट्टे खाते (Write-off) में नहीं डाला जा सकता। यह वस्तु तब तक सरकारी संपत्ति रजिस्टर में बनी रहती है जब तक कि नियमानुसार (नियम 217-219 के तहत) एक सर्वेक्षण समिति द्वारा इसे अनुपयोगी, अप्रचलित या कबाड़ घोषित करके सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा औपचारिक रूप से अपलेखित न कर दिया जाए। अतः कथन (C) गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Non-consumable stores are written off from the register as soon as issued to an employee.

Non-consumable stores represent durable items like computers, furniture, and laboratory apparatus. questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 194 of the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 ('Procurement of Consulting services by nomination'), single-source selection or engagement of a consultant on a nomination basis without open competitive bidding is an exception strictly restricted to special circumstances, such as:
(i) In situations of extreme urgency or emergency, or
(ii) When only a particular consulting firm has exclusive technical ownership or intellectual capability.
Rule 194 specifically provides that in cases of emergency, a Ministry or Department may procure consulting services on a direct nomination basis up to an estimated value of Rs. 2.5 Lakhs (Rupees Two Lakhs and Fifty Thousand only) per occasion, subject to detailed recorded justifications and the prior approval of the competent authority / Head of Department.
